words.enDefinition: A place available for people to use together

examples.en: The new public space has tables where students can work between their afternoon classes.
examples.zh: 新开放的「公共空间」里有桌子，学生下午没课时可以在那里学习。

examples.en: We chose a public space near the library so everyone could get there easily.
examples.zh: 我们选了图书馆附近的一处「公共空间」，这样大家都容易到。

words.enDefinition: A building or place provided for public use

examples.en: We used a public facility near the park for our weekend language exchange.
examples.zh: 周末语言交流活动是在公园附近的一处「公共活动设施」举行的。

examples.en: The town turned the old building into a public facility with meeting rooms.
examples.zh: 镇上把这栋旧楼改成了设有会议室的「公共活动设施」。

words.enDefinition: A hall used for events by local groups

examples.en: We met at the community hall for a book swap on Saturday afternoon.
examples.zh: 我们周六下午在「社区活动大厅」碰面，参加换书活动。

examples.en: The community hall put extra chairs out before the film screening started that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上电影开始放映前，「社区活动大厅」又摆出了一些椅子。

collocations: an event at the community hall

words.enDefinition: A pedestrian path with shelter overhead

examples.en: We took the covered walkway back to the library when it started raining.
examples.zh: 开始下雨时，我们沿着「有顶步行道」回了图书馆。

examples.en: The covered walkway connects two buildings and stays open when the rooms are closed.
examples.zh: 「有顶步行道」连接两栋楼，室内各房间关闭后仍可通行。

words.enDefinition: A narrow way linking areas inside or between buildings

examples.en: We found a passageway behind the main hall that led into the courtyard.
examples.zh: 我们在主厅后面找到一条通向院子的「通道」。

examples.en: The passageway was wide enough for us to walk side by side with our bags.
examples.zh: 这条「通道」足够宽，我们带着包也能并排走。

words.enDefinition: A distinct section extending from a building's main part

examples.en: An entire wing of the building was closed while the volunteers set up the exhibition.
examples.zh: 志愿者布展时，这栋楼有「整个侧翼」暂不开放。

examples.en: I went into the wrong wing of the building and had to cross the courtyard again.
examples.zh: 我进了「这栋楼的另一翼」，只好再穿过院子走回去。

collocations: a new wing of a building
close one wing of the building
a room in the east wing of the building

words.enDefinition: An intermediate floor between two main floors

examples.en: Our group met on the mezzanine above the main doors of the community hall.
examples.zh: 我们小组在社区活动大厅大门上方的「夹层」碰面。

examples.en: The sign near the stairs shows which rooms are on the mezzanine today.
examples.zh: 楼梯旁的指示牌标出了今天「夹层」有哪些房间。

words.enDefinition: An entrance on the side of a building

examples.en: The side entrance was closer to the room where our reading group met.
examples.zh: 「侧门」离读书小组碰面的房间更近。

examples.en: A sign asked visitors to use the side entrance while the front steps were blocked.
examples.zh: 正门台阶无法通行，告示请访客从「侧门」进出。

words.enDefinition: An entrance at the back of a building

examples.en: The rear entrance opens onto the courtyard where volunteers unload chairs for events.
examples.zh: 「后门」通向院子，志愿者在那里卸下活动用的椅子。

examples.en: I found the rear entrance by following the paved path past the garden.
examples.zh: 我沿着铺好的路走过花园，找到了「后门」。

collocations: a sign at the rear entrance

words.enDefinition: A sign that helps people find a place

examples.en: A wayfinding sign near the lift showed which direction led to the meeting rooms.
examples.zh: 电梯旁的「导向指示牌」标出了会议室在哪个方向。

examples.en: I followed a wayfinding sign to the courtyard instead of asking at the desk.
examples.zh: 我跟着「导向指示牌」走到了院子，不用去前台问。

words.enDefinition: A board displaying notices for people to read

examples.en: I checked the noticeboard for the date of the next community book swap.
examples.zh: 我查看了「公告栏」，找下一次社区换书活动的日期。

examples.en: The noticeboard by the entrance had a sheet listing the rooms open that day.
examples.zh: 入口旁的「公告栏」贴了张纸，列出当天开放的房间。

collocations: put up a notice on the noticeboard

words.enDefinition: A map label marking the viewer's current location

examples.en: I looked for the “You are here” dot before trying to locate our meeting room.
examples.zh: 我先找地图上的「您在此处」标记，再找我们要去的会议室。

examples.en: The map's “You are here” marker showed that we were in the east wing.
examples.zh: 地图上的「您在此处」标记显示我们在东翼。

words.enDefinition: A sign identifying a room or its use

examples.en: The room sign said Craft Room, so I knew we had gone one door too far.
examples.zh: 「房间标牌」上写着手工室，我才知道我们多走过了一扇门。

examples.en: I took a picture of the room sign so my classmate could find us.
examples.zh: 我拍下「房间标牌」，方便同学找到我们。

collocations: a room sign on the door

words.enDefinition: An arrow indicating which way someone should go

examples.en: The directional arrow pointed upstairs, although I expected the hall to be straight ahead.
examples.zh: 「方向箭头」指向楼上，可我原以为一直走就能到大厅。

examples.en: I followed the directional arrow past two doors to the smaller meeting room.
examples.zh: 我跟着「方向箭头」走过两扇门，到了较小的会议室。

words.enDefinition: A sign showing the way out

examples.en: I spotted an exit sign above the door at the far end of the hall.
examples.zh: 我在大厅尽头的门上方看见了一个「出口标志」。

examples.en: The exit sign pointed back toward the courtyard rather than into the next room.
examples.zh: 「出口标志」指回院子方向，并没有指向旁边的房间。

collocations: an exit sign above the door

words.enDefinition: The area in front of a building's elevators

examples.en: My classmate waited in the elevator lobby while I checked the room number.
examples.zh: 我去核对房间号时，同学在「电梯厅」等我。

examples.en: The elevator lobby had a sign showing which floors needed a building pass.
examples.zh: 「电梯厅」里有块牌子，标出了哪些楼层需要通行证。

collocations: a sign in the elevator lobby

words.enDefinition: The doors that open for elevator entry and exit

examples.en: I stood to one side until the elevator doors opened and everyone got out.
examples.zh: 我站到一边，等「电梯门」打开，里面的人都出来了。

examples.en: The elevator doors opened on the floor below the room we'd booked for practice.
examples.zh: 「电梯门」在我们预约的练习室下一层开了。

collocations: stand back from the elevator doors
wait for the elevator doors to close

words.enDefinition: A button pressed to summon an elevator

examples.en: I pressed the call button beside the lift and waited for the light.
examples.zh: 我按了电梯旁的「呼梯按钮」，等灯亮起来。

examples.en: The call button was already lit when we reached the lobby after class.
examples.zh: 下课后我们到了门厅时，「呼梯按钮」已经亮着。

collocations: a call button beside the lift

words.enDefinition: A display showing where an elevator is

examples.en: I watched the floor indicator while waiting for the lift outside the meeting rooms.
examples.zh: 我在会议室外等电梯时，看着「电梯楼层显示器」。

examples.en: The floor indicator showed that the lift was already coming down from the top floor.
examples.zh: 「电梯楼层显示器」显示，电梯已经在从顶楼往下走了。

collocations: the floor indicator above the lift doors

words.enDefinition: A continuous set of steps between floors or landings

examples.en: We went up a short flight of stairs to reach the smaller reading area.
examples.zh: 我们上了「一小段楼梯」，到了较小的阅读区。

examples.en: There was one more flight of stairs beyond the door beside the noticeboard.
examples.zh: 公告栏旁那扇门后面还有「一段楼梯」。

collocations: go up a flight of stairs

words.enDefinition: A level space between or at the end of stairs

examples.en: We paused on the stair landing so a group could pass us on their way down.
examples.zh: 我们在「楼梯平台」停了一下，让一群下楼的人先过去。

examples.en: A window on the stair landing let in afternoon light from the courtyard.
examples.zh: 「楼梯平台」上的窗户让午后的阳光从院子照进来。

collocations: a window at the stair landing

words.enDefinition: A rail for holding while walking or climbing

examples.en: I held the handrail as I came down the stairs with my overloaded bag.
examples.zh: 我背着装太满的包下楼时，扶着「扶手」。

examples.en: The handrail ended just before the hallway leading to the public meeting room.
examples.zh: 「扶手」在通往公共会议室的走廊前就到头了。

words.enDefinition: Immediately across from something

examples.en: The room was directly opposite the main door, so we found it right away.
examples.zh: 房间「就在大门的正对面」，我们一下就找到了。

examples.en: I waited on a bench directly opposite the lift while my friend asked for directions.
examples.zh: 朋友去问路时，我在「电梯正对面」的长椅上等着。

words.enDefinition: Very close to the inner side of an entrance

examples.en: The umbrella stand is just inside the door, next to the basket of leaflets.
examples.zh: 伞架「就在刚进门的地方」，挨着装宣传单的篮子。

examples.en: We waited just inside the building until the rain stopped and the courtyard cleared.
examples.zh: 我们在「楼里靠近门口的地方」等到雨停、院子里的人散去。

words.enDefinition: About midway along a passage or route

examples.en: The smaller meeting room is halfway down the corridor on your right.
examples.zh: 沿走廊走到「一半处」，右手边就是小会议室。

examples.en: I saw the refill station halfway down the hall, near the yellow sign.
examples.zh: 我在「大厅往里走到一半处」看到了饮水补给点，就在黄色标牌附近。

words.enDefinition: At the end farthest from the current position

examples.en: There were two spare chairs at the far end of the shared table.
examples.zh: 共用桌子的「另一头」还有两把空椅子。

examples.en: The smaller entrance is at the far end of the courtyard beside the trees.
examples.zh: 较小的入口「在院子的另一头」，挨着几棵树。

collocations: at the far end of the hall

words.enDefinition: To go where signs indicate

examples.en: You can follow the signs to the courtyard from either side of the hall.
examples.zh: 在大厅的任意一侧都可以「跟着指示牌走」，到院子里去。

examples.en: We tried to follow the signs but missed the arrow by the stairs.
examples.zh: 我们想「跟着指示牌走」，却没看到楼梯旁那个箭头。

collocations: follow the signs to the exit

words.enDefinition: To go up or down using the stairs

examples.en: We decided to take the stairs because we only needed to go up one floor.
examples.zh: 我们只需要上一层，就决定「走楼梯」。

examples.en: I asked whether visitors could take the stairs from the hall into the garden.
examples.zh: 我问访客能不能从大厅「走楼梯」到花园里。

collocations: take the stairs to the next floor

words.enDefinition: A door that opens by a sensor or control

examples.en: The automatic door opened as I approached with a stack of books.
examples.zh: 我抱着一摞书走近时，「自动门」打开了。

examples.en: The automatic door was on the left, beside a set of ordinary glass doors.
examples.zh: 「自动门」在左边，挨着一组普通玻璃门。

collocations: an automatic door at the entrance

words.enDefinition: A door that opens by moving sideways

examples.en: I saw the sliding door move to the right when the hall opened.
examples.zh: 大厅开放时，我看到「推拉门」向右移开。

examples.en: The sliding door was wide enough for two people to walk through together.
examples.zh: 这扇「推拉门」足够宽，两个人能并排走过去。

words.enDefinition: Two doors that together close one opening

examples.en: We carried the tables through the double doors at the back of the hall.
examples.zh: 我们从大厅后面的「双扇门」把桌子搬了进去。

examples.en: The guide said to wait outside the double doors until the event ended.
examples.zh: 指引写着要在「双扇门」外等到活动结束。

collocations: open a set of double doors

words.enDefinition: A door with panels rotating around a central point

examples.en: I had never used a revolving door with a bag this big before.
examples.zh: 我以前没拎着这么大的包走过「旋转门」。

examples.en: The revolving door led into the lobby where my flatmate was already waiting.
examples.zh: 「旋转门」通向门厅，室友已经在那里等我。

words.enDefinition: A button that unlocks a door electronically

examples.en: The volunteer pointed to the door release button so we could leave by ourselves.
examples.zh: 志愿者指给我们看「开门解锁按钮」，这样我们可以自己出去。

examples.en: The door release button was beside the coat hooks inside the meeting room.
examples.zh: 「开门解锁按钮」就在会议室里面的挂衣钩旁。

collocations: point out the door release button

words.enDefinition: A buzzer used to signal someone at a door

examples.en: I pressed the door buzzer and waited for a volunteer to let us in.
examples.zh: 我按了「门口呼叫铃」，等志愿者让我们进去。

examples.en: A note by the door buzzer said it was connected to the upstairs desk.
examples.zh: 「门口呼叫铃」旁的便条说，它连的是楼上的前台。

collocations: a sign by the door buzzer

words.enDefinition: A rotating barrier allowing people through one at a time

examples.en: We walked through the turnstile one by one at the exhibition hall entrance.
examples.zh: 我们在展览厅入口处挨个通过「旋转闸机」。

examples.en: The volunteer directed our group to the wider gate beside the turnstile near reception.
examples.zh: 志愿者把我们一行人领到前台附近「旋转闸机」旁较宽的入口。

words.enDefinition: For use by employees or designated workers only

examples.en: The sign said “Staff only,” so I went back to the public entrance.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「仅限工作人员」，我就回到了公众入口。

examples.en: A “Staff only” notice was on the door leading from the hall to the kitchen.
examples.zh: 从大厅通往厨房的门上贴着「仅限工作人员」的告示。

words.enDefinition: For going in rather than coming out

examples.en: The glass door was marked “Entrance only,” so we used the other side to leave.
examples.zh: 玻璃门标着「仅供进入」，我们就从另一侧出去了。

examples.en: I saw “Entrance only” on the left door and joined the line beside it.
examples.zh: 我看到左边的门写着「仅供进入」，就排到旁边的队伍里。

words.enDefinition: For going out rather than coming in

examples.en: I walked around to the other door after seeing the “Exit only” sign.
examples.zh: 看到「仅供离开」的标示后，我绕到了另一扇门。

examples.en: The side door said “Exit only,” but there was another way in from the courtyard.
examples.zh: 侧门写着「仅供离开」，不过从院子还有一个入口。

words.enDefinition: To leave a space free of objects or people

examples.en: The floor was marked “Keep clear” so people could still get through the doorway.
examples.zh: 地上标着「保持通畅」，让人还能从门口通过。

examples.en: A volunteer asked us to keep clear of the gate while it was opening.
examples.zh: 志愿者让我们在门打开时「别挡在门边」。

words.enDefinition: An entrance provided for a limited time

examples.en: We used the temporary entrance while workers were replacing the front doors at the hall.
examples.zh: 大厅正门在更换，我们走了「临时入口」。

examples.en: The temporary entrance was at the far end of the path beyond the courtyard.
examples.zh: 「临时入口」在穿过院子后那条小路的尽头。

collocations: a sign for the temporary entrance

words.enDefinition: To move one story higher in a building

examples.en: We had to go up a floor to find the room listed on the sign.
examples.zh: 我们得「上一层楼」，才能找到标牌上写的房间。

examples.en: Can we go up a floor from here without going through the main lobby?
examples.zh: 我们能从这里直接「上一层楼」，不用经过主门厅吗？

collocations: go up a floor by lift
need to go up a floor
go up a floor from the lobby

words.enDefinition: To keep a door open for others

examples.en: Could you hold the door open while we carry the chairs into the hall?
examples.zh: 我们把椅子搬进大厅时，能请你「扶住门」吗？

examples.en: I stopped to hold the door open for someone carrying a stack of books.
examples.zh: 我停下来替抱着一摞书的人「扶着门没让它关上」。

collocations: hold the door open for someone
offer to hold the door open
stop to hold the door open

words.enDefinition: A space set aside for people to sit

examples.en: We waited in the seating area by the doors while the room was being opened.
examples.zh: 房间还没开门时，我们在门旁的「座位区」等着。

examples.en: The seating area outside the hall was quieter than the one near the entrance.
examples.zh: 大厅外的「座位区」比入口旁的那个安静。

words.enDefinition: A long outdoor seat in a park

examples.en: I found my classmate on a park bench beside the path after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后，我在小路旁的「公园长椅」上找到了同学。

examples.en: The park bench under the tree was still dry after the brief shower.
examples.zh: 那阵短雨停后，树下的「公园长椅」还是干的。

words.enDefinition: An outdoor table used for eating or gathering

examples.en: We spread our notes out on a picnic table while waiting for the hall to open.
examples.zh: 等大厅开门时，我们把笔记摊在一张「野餐桌」上。

examples.en: The picnic table near the path had enough room for all six of us.
examples.zh: 小路旁的「野餐桌」够我们六个人坐。

words.enDefinition: A sheltered place for people to wait

examples.en: We moved to the covered waiting area when the rain started getting heavier.
examples.zh: 雨下得更大时，我们移到了「带顶棚的等候区」。

examples.en: The covered waiting area had a low wall where I could rest my bag.
examples.zh: 「带顶棚的等候区」有一堵矮墙，我可以把包搁上去。

collocations: wait in a covered waiting area
shelter in a covered waiting area

words.enDefinition: Seating arranged on long benches instead of individual chairs

examples.en: The hall uses bench seating along the wall and chairs in the middle.
examples.zh: 大厅沿墙摆的是「长椅式座位」，中间另外摆了椅子。

examples.en: The bench seating near the entrance gave us somewhere to sit during the break.
examples.zh: 入口旁的「长椅式座位」让我们休息时有地方坐。

words.enDefinition: A table used by several people or groups

examples.en: I found space at a shared table and opened my notebook beside another student.
examples.zh: 我在「共用桌」上找到空位，在另一位学生旁边打开笔记本。

examples.en: We left one end of the shared table clear for people who arrived later.
examples.zh: 我们把「共用桌」的一头空出来，留给后面来的人。

words.enDefinition: A seat available for someone else to use

examples.en: I saw a spare seat near the wall and moved closer to the group.
examples.zh: 我看到墙边有个「空余座位」，就往小组那边挪了挪。

examples.en: The volunteer pointed out a spare seat at the end of the front row.
examples.zh: 志愿者指了指出第一排最边上的一个「空余座位」。

collocations: a spare seat at the back

words.enDefinition: A question asking whether a seat is available

examples.en: I asked, “Is this seat taken?” before putting my bag next to the chair.
examples.zh: 把包放到椅子旁前，我问：「这个座位有人吗？」

examples.en: I pointed to the chair beside my classmate and asked, “Is this seat taken?”
examples.zh: 我指着同学旁边的椅子问：「这个座位有人吗？」

words.enDefinition: A polite request for permission to sit somewhere
acceptedEnVariants: do you mind if I sit here

examples.en: I asked the student, “Mind if I sit here while I wait for my friend?”
examples.zh: 我问那位学生：「我坐这里等朋友可以吗？」

examples.en: I asked, “Mind if I sit here?” before joining the people at the shared table.
examples.zh: 我坐到共用桌那群人旁边前，先问：「我坐这里可以吗？」

collocations: reply to “Mind if I sit here?”

words.enDefinition: To shift sideways to leave space for someone

examples.en: Could you move over a little so I can sit next to you?
examples.zh: 你能「往旁边挪一挪」，让我坐在你旁边吗？

examples.en: We had to move over when more people came into the hall after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后更多人进了大厅，我们只好「往旁边挪了挪」。

words.enDefinition: To free space for someone or something

examples.en: We put our bags under the bench to make room for two more people.
examples.zh: 我们把包放在长椅下，「腾出空间」让另外两个人坐。

examples.en: Could we make room for another chair at the end of the shared table?
examples.zh: 我们能在共用桌的尽头「腾个地方」再放把椅子吗？

collocations: move a chair to make room

words.enDefinition: Enough space for one additional person

examples.en: Is there room for one more at the table beside the window over there?
examples.zh: 靠窗那张桌子「还有一个人的位置」吗？

examples.en: The people on the bench said there was room for one more near the end.
examples.zh: 长椅上的人说，靠边那儿「还有一个人的位置」。

words.enDefinition: Having room to stand but no seats left

examples.en: The hall was standing room only by the time we arrived after class.
examples.zh: 我们下课赶到大厅时，「只剩站位」了。

examples.en: A volunteer warned us that the reading would be standing room only by noon.
examples.zh: 志愿者提醒我们，到中午朗读活动就会「只剩站位」。

collocations: end up with standing room only

words.enDefinition: Extra seating for people the main area cannot hold

examples.en: The volunteer directed us to overflow seating when the main room filled up.
examples.zh: 主厅坐满后，志愿者领我们去了「客满时加设的座位」那里。

examples.en: The event had overflow seating in another room with a view of the stage.
examples.zh: 活动在另一间能看到舞台的房间里设了「客满时加设的座位」。

words.enDefinition: The total number of seats available in a space

examples.en: I asked about the seating capacity before booking the hall for our reading group.
examples.zh: 给读书小组预约大厅前，我问了「可容纳的座位数」。

examples.en: The room guide listed the seating capacity for each arrangement of tables and chairs.
examples.zh: 房间指南按桌椅的不同摆法列出了各自「可容纳的座位数」。

words.enDefinition: Holding as many people as can be accommodated

examples.en: The volunteer said the hall was at capacity, so we waited for the next session.
examples.zh: 志愿者说大厅「已满员」，我们就等下一场。

examples.en: The reading room was already at capacity when I checked after my afternoon lecture.
examples.zh: 我下午下课过去看时，阅览室已经「满员」了。

words.enDefinition: To arrange people in a line to wait

examples.en: The volunteer asked us to form a queue along the wall beside the entrance.
examples.zh: 志愿者请我们沿着入口旁的墙「排成一队」。

examples.en: We began to form a queue after the doors opened for the book sale.
examples.zh: 图书义卖开门后，我们开始「排成一队」。

collocations: ask people to form a queue

words.enDefinition: To take a place at the end of a queue

examples.en: We had to join the queue outside because there wasn't enough space in the lobby.
examples.zh: 门厅里地方不够，我们得在外面「加入队伍」。

examples.en: Where should I join the queue for the afternoon event at the community hall?
examples.zh: 要参加社区活动大厅的下午场，我应该在哪儿「加入队伍」？

collocations: join the queue at the back

words.enDefinition: To stay in a queue until it is your turn

examples.en: We had to wait in line to return the chairs after the event.
examples.zh: 活动结束后，我们得「排队等候」归还椅子。

examples.en: I didn't mind having to wait in line because the hall was warm.
examples.zh: 大厅里暖和，我不介意「排队等候」。

collocations: wait in line for a seat

words.enDefinition: A sign marking where people should start queuing

examples.en: The sign said “Queue starts here” next to the rope beside the wall.
examples.zh: 墙边的绳子旁有块牌子，上面写着「请从此处排队」。

examples.en: I looked for “Queue starts here” because two groups were waiting by the door.
examples.zh: 门边有两群人在等，我就找写着「请从此处排队」的牌子。

collocations: a floor sticker reading “Queue starts here”
mark the spot with “Queue starts here”

words.enDefinition: The end of a queue where new people join

examples.en: I went to the back of the line after finding out where it started.
examples.zh: 我弄清从哪儿排队后，就去了「队尾」。

examples.en: My classmate waved from the back of the line near the courtyard gate.
examples.zh: 同学站在院门附近的「队尾」，朝我挥了挥手。

collocations: go to the back of the line
join the back of the line
wait at the back of the line

words.enDefinition: The end of a queue where people are served first

examples.en: I reached the front of the queue just as the volunteer called the next group.
examples.zh: 我刚排到「队头」，志愿者就叫下一组了。

examples.en: From the front of the queue I could see which door had opened.
examples.zh: 在「队头」，我能看到开的是哪扇门。

collocations: reach the front of the queue
stand at the front of the queue
move to the front of the queue

words.enDefinition: To take a place ahead of people already waiting

examples.en: A volunteer reminded visitors not to cut in line when the other door opened.
examples.zh: 另一扇门打开时，志愿者提醒访客不要「插队」。

examples.en: I thought someone was trying to cut in line, but they were just passing through.
examples.zh: 我以为有人要「插队」，其实对方只是路过。

collocations: ask someone not to cut in line
cut in line ahead of someone

words.enDefinition: To keep my spot in the queue while I'm away

examples.en: Could you hold my place while I go back for the umbrella I left inside?
examples.zh: 我进去拿落下的伞时，你能「帮我留一下排队的位置」吗？

examples.en: I asked my classmate to hold my place while I checked the sign.
examples.zh: 我请同学「帮我留住排队的位置」，我去看一下牌子。

collocations: ask someone to hold my place
hold my place for a minute

words.enDefinition: The person whose turn comes next

examples.en: I was next in line when the volunteer took another batch of coats.
examples.zh: 志愿者来取下一批外套时，我正「排在下一位」。

examples.en: My roommate said I was next in line and pointed toward the open desk.
examples.zh: 室友指着开放的服务台，说我「排在下一位」。

collocations: call the person next in line

words.enDefinition: A barrier used to guide a queue

examples.en: The queue barrier curved around the corner so people could still use the stairs.
examples.zh: 「排队隔栏」绕过拐角，这样人们还可以走楼梯。

examples.en: The volunteer moved the queue barrier a little farther from the front doors.
examples.zh: 志愿者把「排队隔栏」往离大门稍远的地方挪了一点。

words.enDefinition: A mark on the floor showing a position

examples.en: I stood on the floor marker while the volunteer checked who was next.
examples.zh: 志愿者查看轮到谁时，我站在「地面标记」上等着。

examples.en: The floor marker near the doorway showed where the line should begin that morning.
examples.zh: 那天早上，门口附近的「地面标记」指明了从哪里开始排队。

collocations: a floor marker beside the entrance

words.enDefinition: A polite direction to stay in this spot

examples.en: A sign reading “Please wait here” stood by the entrance to the smaller room.
examples.zh: 较小房间的入口旁立着一块牌子，上面写着「请在此等候」。

examples.en: The volunteer said, “Please wait here until I check whether the hall is ready.”
examples.zh: 志愿者请我们「在此等候」，他要先看看大厅准备好了没有。

words.enDefinition: A machine giving numbered slips to people waiting

examples.en: The ticket dispenser was beside the door where people came into the hall.
examples.zh: 「排队取号机」就在大家进大厅的那扇门旁边。

examples.en: I took a slip from the ticket dispenser and sat near the display.
examples.zh: 我从「排队取号机」拿了张号码纸，坐在显示屏旁。

collocations: take a slip from the ticket dispenser
a ticket dispenser by the entrance

words.enDefinition: To stay until one's name or number is called

examples.en: We were told to wait to be called after taking a slip from the machine.
examples.zh: 我们从机器取号后，对方让我们「等候叫号」。

examples.en: I sat near the doorway to wait to be called for my turn.
examples.zh: 我坐在门口附近「等候叫号」，等轮到自己。

collocations: sit down and wait to be called
wait to be called by number
wait to be called by name

words.enDefinition: Given to people in the order they arrive

examples.en: The sign said seats were first come, first served, so we got there early.
examples.zh: 告示说座位「先到先得」，所以我们早到了。

examples.en: Tickets were first come, first served at the community hall that Saturday afternoon.
examples.zh: 那周六下午，社区活动大厅的票「先到先得」。

collocations: first come first served at the door
first come first served for a seat

words.enDefinition: To move to one side of a space

examples.en: I had to step aside when the volunteer came through with a stack of chairs.
examples.zh: 志愿者搬着一摞椅子过来时，我得「往旁边站开」。

examples.en: Could you step aside for a moment so I can get past with these chairs?
examples.zh: 你能「往旁边站开」一下，让我搬着这些椅子过去吗？

collocations: step aside to let someone pass

words.enDefinition: To move or allow space for someone to pass

examples.en: We had to let someone through before we could close the double doors.
examples.zh: 我们得先「让一个人通过」，才能关上双扇门。

examples.en: Can you let someone through if they need to reach the stairs behind you?
examples.zh: 如果有人要去你身后的楼梯，你能「让人通过」吗？

collocations: move aside to let someone through
open the gate to let someone through

words.enDefinition: To keep enough space for people to move past

examples.en: We moved the bags closer to the wall to leave room to pass.
examples.zh: 我们把包往墙边挪了挪，「留出通行空间」。

examples.en: The volunteer asked everyone to leave room to pass between the tables and the door.
examples.zh: 志愿者请大家在桌子和门之间「留出通行空间」。

collocations: remember to leave room to pass
move aside to leave room to pass

words.enDefinition: To stay on the left side while moving

examples.en: The sign asked everyone to keep to the left when entering the hall.
examples.zh: 告示请大家进大厅时「靠左走」。

examples.en: We tried to keep to the left so people walking out could pass.
examples.zh: 我们尽量「靠左走」，让往外走的人能过去。

collocations: keep to the left on the stairs
a sign saying keep to the left
keep to the left of the hallway

words.enDefinition: The movement or number of people on foot

examples.en: The doorway had a lot of foot traffic just after the afternoon event ended.
examples.zh: 下午的活动刚结束，门口的「行人流量」很大。

examples.en: We chose a table away from heavy foot traffic so we could hear each other.
examples.zh: 我们找了张桌子，避开「行人来往密集」的地方，这样能听清彼此说话。

collocations: direct foot traffic away from an entrance

words.enDefinition: The busiest hours at a particular place or service

examples.en: The courtyard gets crowded during peak hours when two classes finish around the same time.
examples.zh: 两节课差不多同时结束的「高峰时段」，院子里会很挤。

examples.en: I avoided the hall during peak hours so I could find a quiet seat.
examples.zh: 为了找个安静座位，我避开「高峰时段」去大厅。

collocations: open an extra door during peak hours

words.enDefinition: Hours when a place or service is less busy

examples.en: We visited during off-peak hours and had the back of the hall to ourselves.
examples.zh: 我们在「非高峰时段」去了大厅，整个后半区就我们在用。

examples.en: I asked which off-peak hours would be best for our small reading group.
examples.zh: 我问我们的读书小组选哪个「非高峰时段」比较合适。

words.enDefinition: An area where people are expected to make little noise

examples.en: I took my phone into the hallway because we were sitting in a quiet area.
examples.zh: 我们坐的是「安静区」，所以我拿着手机去了走廊。

examples.en: The sign by the stairs showed which part of the building was a quiet area.
examples.zh: 楼梯旁的告示标出了楼里哪片是「安静区」。

words.enDefinition: To avoid making too much noise

examples.en: Could you keep the noise down while the group next door finishes its discussion?
examples.zh: 隔壁小组还在讨论，你们能「小声一点」吗？

examples.en: The sign asked visitors to keep the noise down near the smaller rooms.
examples.zh: 告示请访客在那些小房间附近「小声一点」。

collocations: ask people to keep the noise down
try to keep the noise down
keep the noise down in the hallway

words.enDefinition: A notice that the room is occupied

examples.en: The sign on the door said “Room in use,” so we waited outside.
examples.zh: 门上的牌子写着「房间使用中」，我们就在外面等。

examples.en: When I saw “Room in use,” I went upstairs to find an empty space.
examples.zh: 看到「房间使用中」后，我就上楼找空地方了。

collocations: mark a room as in use
a door notice reading “Room in use”

words.zhGloss: 离开时把房间收拾整齐
words.enDefinition: To make sure a room is neat when leaving
acceptedZhAnswers: 离开时把房间收拾整齐

examples.en: The notice asked us to leave the room tidy after the weekly language exchange.
examples.zh: 告示请我们每周语言交流结束后「把房间收拾整齐再离开」。

examples.en: We took our cups away and put the chairs back to leave the room tidy.
examples.zh: 我们拿走杯子，把椅子放回原位，离开前「把房间收拾整齐」。

collocations: remember to leave the room tidy
ask users to leave the room tidy

words.enDefinition: Closed for a short period of time

examples.en: The courtyard was temporarily closed while volunteers set up for the afternoon event.
examples.zh: 志愿者为下午的活动布置场地时，院子「暂时关闭」。

examples.en: I saw “Temporarily closed” on the sign and waited by the side entrance.
examples.zh: 我看到牌子上写着「暂时关闭」，就在侧门旁边等。

words.enDefinition: Unavailable because repair or upkeep is taking place

examples.en: The smaller hall was closed for maintenance, so we met in the courtyard.
examples.zh: 小厅「因维护暂停开放」，我们就在院子里见面了。

examples.en: The notice said the fountain was closed for maintenance until the following Monday.
examples.zh: 告示说，喷泉「因维护暂停开放」，要到下周一才恢复。

words.enDefinition: Not working and therefore unusable

examples.en: The lift was out of order, so we waited downstairs for the others.
examples.zh: 电梯「出了故障」，我们就在楼下等其他人。

examples.en: I found a note saying the hand dryer was out of order that morning.
examples.zh: 那天早上我看到一张便条，上面说烘手机「发生了故障」。

words.enDefinition: Available again after an interruption

examples.en: The lift was back in service when I came to the hall after lunch.
examples.zh: 我午饭后来到大厅时，电梯已经「恢复使用」。

examples.en: The volunteer said the bottle filler would be back in service by the next event.
examples.zh: 志愿者说，自助饮水补给机到下次活动时会「恢复使用」。

collocations: put a lift back in service

words.enDefinition: Available for anyone to enter or use

examples.en: The courtyard is open to the public even when the meeting rooms are locked.
examples.zh: 即使会议室锁了，院子也「向公众开放」。

examples.en: I asked whether the hall was open to the public during the weekend.
examples.zh: 我问大厅周末是否「向公众开放」。

collocations: open to the public on weekdays

words.enDefinition: Opening times displayed on a sign or notice

examples.en: I checked the posted hours before asking my classmate to meet me there.
examples.zh: 约同学在那里见面之前，我看了「公示的开放时间」。

examples.en: The posted hours on the door were different from the ones on the website.
examples.zh: 门上「公示的开放时间」和网站上的不一样。

words.enDefinition: A schedule in which a place opens for less time

examples.en: The hall had reduced opening hours while most of the volunteers were away.
examples.zh: 大部分志愿者不在时，大厅按「缩短后的开放时间」开放。

examples.en: I checked the reduced opening hours before planning our evening reading group that week.
examples.zh: 安排那周晚上的读书小组活动前，我核对了「缩短后的开放时间」。

collocations: reduced opening hours during the holidays

words.enDefinition: The latest time people can enter a place

examples.en: The sign said last entry was at four, although the doors closed later.
examples.zh: 牌子写着「最晚入场时间」是四点，关门时间要晚一些。

examples.en: I asked about last entry because my class would not finish until late afternoon.
examples.zh: 我的课要到下午很晚才下课，所以我问了「最晚入场时间」。

words.zhGloss: 暂停开放直至另行通知
words.enDefinition: Closed with no reopening date given yet
acceptedZhAnswers: 暂停开放直至另行通知

examples.en: The notice said the courtyard was closed until further notice after the weekend storm.
examples.zh: 周末暴风雨过后，告示说院子「暂停开放直至另行通知」。

examples.en: The reading area was closed until further notice, so our group met outdoors instead.
examples.zh: 阅读区「暂停开放直至另行通知」，我们小组就改在室外见面了。

collocations: a Closed until further notice sign

words.enDefinition: Separated by a barrier to keep people out

examples.en: The corner by the hall was cordoned off while volunteers moved the heavy display.
examples.zh: 志愿者搬移沉重的展台时，大厅旁的那个角落「被围起来禁止通行」。

examples.en: We saw that part of the courtyard was cordoned off, so we walked around it.
examples.zh: 我们发现院子的一部分「被围了起来」，就绕过去了。

words.enDefinition: A sign warning that the floor is wet

examples.en: I noticed the wet floor sign before stepping into the lobby with my books.
examples.zh: 我抱着书走进门厅前，注意到了「小心地滑警示牌」。

examples.en: The volunteer put a wet floor sign beside the entrance after the rain started.
examples.zh: 开始下雨后，志愿者在入口旁放了一块「小心地滑警示牌」。

collocations: put out a wet floor sign
walk past a wet floor sign

words.enDefinition: Permission to enter with some restrictions

examples.en: The notice said there was limited access to the courtyard during the afternoon event.
examples.zh: 告示说，下午活动期间，院子「通行受限」。

examples.en: I asked what limited access meant because our group needed only one meeting room.
examples.zh: 我们小组只需要一间会议室，所以我问「有限通行」具体指什么。

collocations: have limited access to a building

words.enDefinition: A fixture designed for refilling drinking water bottles

examples.en: I used the bottle-filling station near the stairs before leaving for my next class.
examples.zh: 我去上下一节课前，在楼梯旁的「饮用水加水点」接了水。

examples.en: The sign showed a bottle-filling station on the next floor near the meeting room.
examples.zh: 标牌显示，楼上一层的会议室旁有一个「饮用水加水点」。

words.enDefinition: A small enclosed space containing one toilet

examples.en: I noticed a small hook inside the toilet cubicle for hanging my coat.
examples.zh: 我看到「卫生间隔间」里面有个小钩子，可以挂外套。

examples.en: The light above the toilet cubicle was on when I walked into the washroom.
examples.zh: 我走进洗手间时，「卫生间隔间」上方的灯亮着。

collocations: a lock on a toilet cubicle

words.enDefinition: A restroom available to people of any gender

examples.en: The map showed an all-gender restroom next to the drinking water station.
examples.zh: 地图标出饮水补给点旁有一个「不限性别的洗手间」。

examples.en: I asked the volunteer where the all-gender restroom was before the screening began.
examples.zh: 放映开始前，我问志愿者「不限性别的洗手间」在哪儿。

words.enDefinition: A surface for changing a baby's diaper

examples.en: The community hall had a baby changing station in the larger washroom near reception.
examples.zh: 社区活动大厅靠近前台的那个大洗手间里有「婴儿换尿布台」。

examples.en: My classmate checked the map for a baby changing station before bringing her nephew.
examples.zh: 同学带侄子来之前，看地图确认哪里有「婴儿换尿布台」。

words.enDefinition: A machine blowing air to dry hands

examples.en: The hand dryer started when I moved my hands under it in the washroom.
examples.zh: 我在洗手间把手放到「烘手机」下面时，它启动了。

examples.en: I hung my bag on a hook near the hand dryer while I waited.
examples.zh: 等候时，我把包挂在「烘手机」旁的挂钩上。

words.enDefinition: A container releasing a portion of soap

examples.en: The soap dispenser beside the left sink was empty when I checked.
examples.zh: 我看了一下，左边洗手池旁的「皂液器」空了。

examples.en: The sign pointed to a soap dispenser on the wall between two sinks.
examples.zh: 标牌指向两个洗手池之间的墙上一个「皂液器」。

words.enDefinition: A holder that dispenses paper towels for drying hands

examples.en: I found the paper towel dispenser on the wall behind the washroom door.
examples.zh: 我在洗手间门后的墙上找到了「擦手纸盒」。

examples.en: The paper towel dispenser was empty, so I used the hand dryer instead.
examples.zh: 「擦手纸盒」空了，我就改用烘手机。

words.enDefinition: A sign showing that a space is already occupied

examples.en: I saw an occupied sign on the cubicle door and waited by the sinks.
examples.zh: 我看到隔间门上有「有人使用的标示」，就到洗手池旁边等。

examples.en: The occupied sign turned red when I locked the cubicle door from inside.
examples.zh: 我从里面锁上隔间门时，「有人使用的标示」变成了红色。

words.enDefinition: A bin with a lid operated by a pedal

examples.en: The foot pedal bin fit under the counter next to the washroom door.
examples.zh: 「脚踏垃圾桶」放得进洗手间门旁的台面下。

examples.en: I dropped my paper towel into the foot pedal bin before leaving the washroom.
examples.zh: 离开洗手间前，我把擦手纸扔进了「脚踏垃圾桶」。

words.enDefinition: A place with separate bins for recyclable materials

examples.en: I carried the empty cans to the recycling station outside the community hall.
examples.zh: 我把空罐拿到社区活动大厅外面的「垃圾分类回收点」。

examples.en: The recycling station had pictures showing which bins were for paper and bottles.
examples.zh: 「垃圾分类回收点」有图示，标明哪些桶收纸张、哪些收瓶子。

words.enDefinition: A holder for umbrellas near an entrance

examples.en: I left my wet umbrella in the umbrella stand just inside the door.
examples.zh: 我把湿伞放在刚进门的「伞架」上。

examples.en: The umbrella stand was full after the group arrived in the afternoon rain.
examples.zh: 下午下着雨，那群人到齐后，「伞架」就放满了。

collocations: leave an umbrella in the umbrella stand
an umbrella stand by the door

words.enDefinition: A hook used for hanging a coat

examples.en: I found a coat hook behind the door and hung my raincoat there.
examples.zh: 我在门后找到一个「挂衣钩」，就把雨衣挂在那儿。

examples.en: The coat hook by my seat was already holding two jackets and a bag.
examples.zh: 我座位旁的「挂衣钩」上已经挂了两件夹克和一个包。

collocations: hang a coat on a coat hook

words.enDefinition: A service that keeps visitors' coats during an event

examples.en: I left my coat at the coat check before walking into the hall.
examples.zh: 我进大厅前把外套留在了「外套寄存处」。

examples.en: The volunteer at the coat check handed me a ticket with my number.
examples.zh: 「外套寄存处」的志愿者递给我一张写着号码的票。

collocations: leave a jacket at coat check
pick up a coat from coat check

words.enDefinition: A locker for storing belongings during the day

examples.en: I put my backpack in a day locker before entering the small exhibition.
examples.zh: 我进去看小型展览前，把背包放进了一个「当日使用的储物柜」。

examples.en: The day locker was just big enough for my coat and course notes.
examples.zh: 这个「当日使用的储物柜」刚好能放下我的外套和课程笔记。

words.enDefinition: A key that locks or opens a locker

examples.en: I kept the locker key in my pocket until the afternoon event ended.
examples.zh: 下午的活动结束前，我把「储物柜钥匙」放在口袋里。

examples.en: The volunteer asked me to return the locker key when I collected my bag.
examples.zh: 我回来取包时，志愿者请我归还「储物柜钥匙」。

words.enDefinition: A small open compartment used for storing belongings

examples.en: I slid my backpack into a storage cubby before taking a seat in the hall.
examples.zh: 我先把背包塞进一个「开放式储物格」，再在大厅找了个座位。

examples.en: The storage cubby by the door was wide enough for my bike helmet.
examples.zh: 门旁的「开放式储物格」够宽，能放下我的自行车头盔。

collocations: place a bag in a storage cubby

words.enDefinition: Something misplaced by its owner and discovered by someone

examples.en: The volunteer labelled the found item with the date and place it was discovered.
examples.zh: 志愿者给「拾获物品」贴了标签，写明捡到的日期和地点。

examples.en: I told the desk where I had picked up the found item after class.
examples.zh: 我下课后告诉前台，自己是在哪里捡到这件「拾获物品」的。

words.enDefinition: A locker with a connection for charging phones

examples.en: I put my phone in a phone charging locker while I joined the reading group.
examples.zh: 我参加读书小组活动时，把手机放在「手机充电储物柜」里。

examples.en: The hall had a phone charging locker with a separate key for each compartment.
examples.zh: 大厅有一个「手机充电储物柜」，每一格都有单独的钥匙。

collocations: a compartment in a phone charging locker

words.enDefinition: Wireless internet offered for general public use

examples.en: I connected to the public Wi-Fi to check which room our group had booked.
examples.zh: 我连上「公共无线网」，查看我们小组预约了哪个房间。

examples.en: The sign on the wall gave the name of the public Wi-Fi network.
examples.zh: 墙上的标牌写了「公共无线网」的名称。

words.enDefinition: A page displayed before internet access is granted

examples.en: I opened the Wi-Fi sign-in page when the network did not connect automatically.
examples.zh: 网络没自动连上时，我打开了「无线网登录页面」。

examples.en: The Wi-Fi sign-in page appeared after I selected the community hall's guest network.
examples.zh: 我选了社区活动大厅的访客网络后，「无线网登录页面」就弹出来了。

collocations: instructions on the Wi-Fi sign-in page

words.enDefinition: A machine that sells items without an attendant

examples.en: I bought a bottle of water from the vending machine beside the smaller hall.
examples.zh: 我在小厅旁的「自动售货机」买了一瓶水。

examples.en: The vending machine near the entrance had a small shelf for collecting drinks.
examples.zh: 入口旁的「自动售货机」有个取饮料的小托架。

collocations: buy something from a vending machine

words.enDefinition: A printer made available for public use

examples.en: I found a public printer in the community centre after leaving my notes at home.
examples.zh: 我把笔记忘在家里，后来在社区中心找到一台「公用打印机」。

examples.en: The volunteer showed me where to collect the pages from the public printer.
examples.zh: 志愿者指给我看从「公用打印机」哪里取纸。

collocations: a public printer near the desk

words.enDefinition: A spoken message played over a loudspeaker system

examples.en: The overhead announcement said the afternoon group should move to the other entrance.
examples.zh: 「公共广播」说下午场那一组应该换到另一个入口。

examples.en: We heard an overhead announcement just as the doors to the hall opened.
examples.zh: 大厅门刚一打开，我们就听到了一段「公共广播」。

words.enDefinition: A screen showing information that can be updated

examples.en: The digital display near the door showed which rooms were open that evening.
examples.zh: 门旁的「电子显示屏」标出了那天晚上哪些房间开放。

examples.en: We watched the digital display until our group number appeared beside the room name.
examples.zh: 我们看着「电子显示屏」，直到组号出现在房间名称旁。

words.enDefinition: A folding sign with two panels forming an A shape

examples.en: The volunteer put an A-frame sign outside to point people toward the side entrance.
examples.zh: 志愿者在外面放了一个「A字形立式标牌」，给人们指明侧门的方向。

examples.en: The A-frame sign was moved indoors when the wind began picking up outside.
examples.zh: 外面的风大起来时，那个「A字形立式标牌」被挪进了室内。

collocations: an A-frame sign on the path

words.enDefinition: A mat designed to reduce slipping

examples.en: The volunteer laid a non-slip mat inside the entrance after it began raining.
examples.zh: 下雨后，志愿者在入口内侧铺了一张「防滑垫」。

examples.en: I put my umbrella aside and stepped onto the non-slip mat by the door.
examples.zh: 我把伞放到一边，踩上了门边的「防滑垫」。

words.enDefinition: A light that responds to nearby movement

examples.en: The motion-sensor light came on as I walked into the empty hallway.
examples.zh: 我走进空荡荡的走廊时，「感应灯」亮了。

examples.en: A motion-sensor light above the door made it easier to read the room sign.
examples.zh: 门上的「感应灯」让房间标牌更容易看清。

words.enDefinition: Tape stretched across a space to restrict entry

examples.en: The volunteers put barrier tape across one side of the courtyard during the setup.
examples.zh: 布置场地时，志愿者在院子的一侧拉起了「警戒隔离带」。

examples.en: The barrier tape was gone when we came back after the afternoon session.
examples.zh: 我们下午场结束后回来时，「警戒隔离带」已经拆掉了。

collocations: an area marked off with barrier tape

words.enDefinition: Not open during the lunch break

examples.en: The reception area was closed for lunch, so we waited on a bench nearby.
examples.zh: 接待区「午休暂停开放」，我们就在附近长椅上等。

examples.en: I saw the “Closed for lunch” sign when I went back to collect my bag.
examples.zh: 我回去拿包时，看到了「午休暂停开放」的牌子。
